comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue increased to 49% in 2024 from 46% in 2023. This increase was primarily driven by a favorable shift in revenue mix towards higher Data Center and Client revenues, as well as lower Gaming revenue, which was partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD report an increase in overall gross margin for fiscal year 2024 compared to 2023, driven by strong Data Center demand. NVDA’s gross margin rose significantly to 72.7% from 56.9%, attributed to 217% Data Center revenue growth and lower inventory provisions. AMD’s gross margin increased to 49% from 46%, primarily driven by a favorable revenue mix shift toward higher Data Center revenues. While both cite Data Center growth as a key driver, NVDA experienced a much larger margin expansion (15.8 percentage points) compared to AMD (3 percentage points), and NVDA specifically highlights lower inventory provisions as a contributor, whereas AMD emphasizes product mix.

sentences.text: Our overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023.
The year over year increase was primarily due to strong Data Center revenue growth of 217% and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue was 49% in 2024 compared to 46% in 2023.
The increase in gross margin was due to a favorable shift in revenue mix of higher Data Center and Client revenues, lower Gaming revenue, partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.

comparisons.peer_topic: Gross margin financial results and VMware impact
comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin increased to $32,509 million in fiscal year 2024 from $24,690 million in fiscal year 2023, primarily due to VMware contributions offset by higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets. As a percentage of net revenue, gross margin decreased to 63% from 69%, driven by the same amortization factors, less favorable semiconductor product mix, and offsets from infrastructure software margins.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and AVGO both report changes in gross margin for fiscal year 2024 compared to 2023, but with contrasting percentage trends and drivers. NVDA’s gross margin increased to 72.7% from 56.9%, driven by Data Center revenue growth and lower inventory provisions. In contrast, AVGO’s gross margin as a percentage of net revenue decreased to 63% from 69%, despite an increase in absolute gross margin dollars ($32.5 billion vs $24.7 billion), driven by higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the VMware Merger and less favorable semiconductor product mix. NVDA’s margin expansion is driven by operational efficiency and product demand, while AVGO’s margin contraction is driven by accounting charges and mix shifts.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, aided by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, despite the prior year's inventory write-downs and lower costs from selling previously written-down inventory in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and MU both report a significant improvement in gross margin for fiscal year 2024 compared to 2023. NVDA’s gross margin increased to 72.7% from 56.9%, driven by Data Center revenue growth and lower inventory provisions. MU’s consolidated gross margin improved to 22% from -9%, driven by higher average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, as well as the effect of prior year inventory write-downs. Both companies faced inventory-related issues in the prior year (NVDA with provisions, MU with write-downs) which negatively impacted their 2023 margins, and both saw margin recovery in 2024 due to mitigating those prior pressures.
